positions.name: ReproAndConstraint
positions.frame: how does a test case encode both the production failure it reproduces and the behavioral constraint it must satisfy?
positions.why: src-1 names the concrete failure pattern the test mirrors (a ## heading with no id field from prod), while src-2 states the non-negotiable behavioral constraint the system must meet when facing that pattern (must not crash, must produce a valid slug). The two expressions cohere under one directional read: a reproduction test asserts both what went wrong and what correct behavior looks like. The conviction gradient — src-1 a flat claim, src-2 a settled decision — is the natural shape of a test specification: observation of the defect, then the rule it demands.
